title: Appar answers the king
hookLine: a king summons a temple singer, and Appar sends back a song: we are subjects of no one. why Shaivas say namah shivaya
carry: namah shivaya: we belong to shiva, not to fear
tomorrow: the youngest of the three singers.

lines: AN OLD MAN WITH A HOE.
cards: A messenger arrives with an order from the king: come to court. The man being summoned is a singer of Shiva, carrying a small hoe, the kind used to pull grass from between the stones of a temple courtyard.
The stories call him Appar. Then, instead of packing a bag, he answers with a song. Its opening, in paraphrase: we are subjects of no one, and we do not fear death.
The messenger goes back carrying a hymn instead of a prisoner.

teach.h: A SUMMONS THAT IS A THREAT
teach.b: Appar's life is told in the Periya Puranam, the book of the lives of the Shaiva saints. It says he spent a long time on another path and then came home to Shiva, and that the king was angry about it.
So the order is a threat, not an invitation.
The song, in paraphrase: we are no one's subjects, we do not fear death, we will not suffer in hell, we do not tremble, we know no sickness, we bow to no one, because we belong to the Lord.
This isn't a protest against kings in general. It's a statement about belonging. If his whole life is Shiva's, there's no room left for a second master.
Then look at the hoe. The man who bows to no king spends his days on his knees, pulling weeds from temple stones so others can walk there barefoot.
Tradition says the king had him tied to a heavy stone and thrown into the sea, and that Appar sang the five syllables, namah shivaya, and the stone floated him to shore.
Some take that as a plain miracle; others hear a picture of what the name of Shiva can hold up. Here's the teaching.
Those five syllables, the panchakshara, are the heart mantra of Shaivas, said at home, in temples, on prayer beads, every day.

teach.h: NAMAH SHIVAYA: WHOM YOU BELONG TO
teach.b: Namah shivaya means bowing to Shiva. Say it, and you've said whom you belong to. Which voice do you finally answer to?

how: In Tamil Shaiva temples, singers called oduvars sing hymns of the Tevaram, including Appar's, during worship, and Appar is often shown in images carrying his small hoe.

games.q: you're Appar. a messenger brings the angry king's order: come to court. what do you do?
o: send back a song: we are subjects of no one.
games.why: he answers with a hymn that says he belongs to the Lord and bows to no one, and the messenger carries the song back.

practice: Notice the voices that summon you today, a message, a deadline, somebody's opinion, and name them one at a time without pushing them away. Then ask quietly: under all of these, what do I answer to in the end?
Let the answer be a word, a person, a promise, or God, and if you pray, say the five syllables Appar sang, namah shivaya, slowly with the breath.
